chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr, who said:

A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about a woman who left behind a husband, maternal siblings, and a paternal sister. He said: 'For the husband is half, three shares; for the maternal siblings is two shares; and for the paternal sister is one share.'

The man said to him: 'Indeed, the rulings of Zayd, and the rulings of the general public and the judges, are not like this, O Abu Ja'far. They say for the paternal sister is three shares, which becomes from six, and it increases (ta'ul) to eight.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And why did they say that?'
He said: 'Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "And if he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left."'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If the sister were a brother?'
He said: 'Then he would not have except one-sixth.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'So why have you reduced the brother's share if you are arguing for the sister's half on the basis that Allah named for her the half? Indeed, Allah has named for the brother the whole, and the whole is more than the half, because He said: "Then for her is the half," and He said regarding the brother: "And he inherits her," meaning all her wealth, "If she has no child."'
So you do not give that which Allah has made for him as the whole, in some of your rulings, anything, and you give that which Allah has made for him as the half, completely.'
The man said to him: 'May Allah rectify you. So how is the sister given the half, while the male is not given anything, if she were a male?'

He said: 'They say in the case of a mother, husband, maternal siblings, and paternal sisters, so they give the husband half, and for the mother one-sixth, and for the maternal siblings one-third, and for the paternal sister half, three shares. So they make it from nine, while it is from six, so it rises to nine.'
He said: 'If the sister were a male, a brother from the father?'
The man said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'So what do you say?'
He said: 'For the paternal siblings, and the maternal siblings, and the siblings from the father and mother, with the mother, is nothing.'

key_terms.اَلْأُخْتُ مِنَ اَلْأَبِ: Paternal sister (sister sharing only the father)
key_terms.تَعُولُ: Increases (the total number of shares exceeds the base number of six)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on the inheritance of a paternal sister when the deceased leaves a husband, mother, and maternal siblings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the prevailing Sunni practice of 'ta'ul' (raising the denominator) by arguing that the Quranic verse for the brother ('He inherits her') implies the entirety of the estate, whereas the sister's verse specifies only half, thus justifying a fixed six-part division without inflation. He further establishes the principle of 'hujb' (exclusion) for paternal and maternal siblings when the mother is present, a view distinct from the majority who grant them shares, highlighting the Shia reliance on precise textual interpretation over analogical reasoning.
